SessionStart._comment: startup and resume ONLY. SessionStart also fires on 'compact', 'clear' and 'fork' — all of which happen mid-conversation on the SAME machine, where there is nothing to restore. Pulling then is at best wasted work and at worst writes over files the running session is using.

UserPromptSubmit._comment: 0.5.7: the prompt that claims the restart also runs the live relink (rcRestore.liveRelink: stale links of sessions with no CLI are cleared first; up to three hidden PowerShell process listings), hence the 30 second timeout; every other prompt still exits at the claim. 0.5.4, Remote Control restore: the first real prompt of an interactive session after a restart of the Claude app gets a one-time instruction to wake the other sessions (rcRestore.wake). Not SessionStart: a session that starts is not yet a session the user is talking to. The command claims the restart with an exclusive file create, so one session acts; it answers nothing and exits at once for every other prompt, on every OS (Windows only acts). The second command (artifact-hook.mjs wake) is the artifact share: when a browser reachable from the session's account can send or accept an artifact queued by the PostToolUse hook below (entries 2+ minutes old, once per 30 minutes per account), one session (claimed with an exclusive file create) gets an instruction to run the share-artifacts skill. It is its own small entry point, not cli.mjs, so a prompt with nothing pending costs a directory listing and a few small reads; any error exits 0 with no output.

PostToolUse._comment: Artifact share: a publish with no url (a new artifact, including one made from a type_url) is appended to ~/.claude/session-sync/artifact-queue/. Reads, lists, updates, asset uploads and deletes are ignored. Prints nothing.

SessionEnd._comment: Hooks fire PER CONVERSATION, not per client. 'clear' is excluded: clearing context is not finishing work, and it would push on every /clear. 'resume' IS included, deliberately and after a reversal. It was dropped on 2026-09-07 on the assumption that a resumed conversation always fires a later, non-resume SessionEnd — but Claude Code's docs guarantee no such thing. If a conversation's ONLY SessionEnd ever fires with reason=resume (app force-closed or crashed after a resume), excluding it means that conversation's final state NEVER reaches the remote. That is the one failure this plugin exists to prevent, so the redundant fires are absorbed instead of avoided: a hook-triggered push now RECORDS a request and coalesces onto a single background worker rather than running (or dropping) one per fire — see lib/defer.mjs. The pull/push/pull triplet inside 0.7s that motivated the removal now costs one recorded request, not a lost push. Restored 2026-09-07.
